title: Tired of teaching and drawn to New York
summary: Waters left Boston because he was tired of teaching, had big-band ambitions, and like many musicians wanted the stamp that New York gave.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: PS: When did you figure out that you were gonna leave the Boston area, what was your thinking behind that and what made you go back to the Philadelphia area briefly?

The only reason I did that, because I got tired of teaching, which is the - teaching is a complicated affair, anyone who teaches knows that. I got tired of teaching, you know, just tired of teaching, not - I was, I could stay there and make much money. But

I'd be working hard, I'd be working at night, I'd be working in the day with the pupils, I'd be working at night and so on and so on and so on, you know. I, it was, I got tired of the pupil, and then I had big band ideas, too, at that period, see. And then I had a little ambition of tryin' to gettin' on top. And then another thing, I think every musician in the whole world - I'll say in the States, not every mu-, but a big portion of musicians wanted to come to New York. They called it "The Apple", you dig, they wanted to come to New York. Not only that, most of the musicians that on top came here to get a stamp. Even Louie Armstrong, as big as Chicago is, the third, the second biggest city of the States, but he didn't make it a real stamp until he came to New York, that's where he got that real stamp. And all those guys, Charlie Parker, for an instance, played in the Kansas City for years as I understand by Jay McShann. But he didn't get his stamp until he came to New York, he's not from New York but he got his stamp here. All these guys that you hear blowin' like hell and all the big time, they got their stamp right here in New York. Because, you know why, it's a mecca. I'm not criticizing New Orleans now, see, because, I'm not criticizing it -
